summary: 7 Wonders Duel reworks the drafting of its parent game into a tight two-player card-tableau battle, with cards laid out face-up and face-down in a pyramid so timing which card to grab (and which you deny your opponent) matters as much as what it does. Games can end abruptly via military or science victory well before the scoring phase, which makes it feel sharper and more confrontational than the original.
praised: excellent, tense two-player design with real head-to-head interaction
sudden-death military and science win conditions create real tension
fast to teach and play at around 30 minutes
criticised: military track can feel punishing if you fall behind early
less variance/variety than the multiplayer original for some tastes
first-player advantage debates in some editions/expansions

interaction.kind: direct card denial and open conflict
interaction.detail: Players draft from a single shared card pyramid where taking a card can deny it to the opponent, and both a shared military track and shared science track can trigger an instant win, making almost every choice directly affect the other player rather than just your own tableau.

scoring.why: The game can end instantly via military supremacy or completing six different science symbols, and if neither triggers, points are tallied across military, science, coins, and several building/wonder categories.
scoring.how_you_win: You win immediately by pushing the military marker to your opponent's capital or by collecting six distinct science symbols; otherwise the player with more total points across all categories at the end of Age III wins.
